questions.q: Which of your hosted services depend on a platform licence that is changing or ending, and by when?
questions.why: A licence change upstream is a date that decides the provider's whole roadmap.
questions.need: Services that depend on a changing licence are listed with dates
questions.how: List hosted services with the platform under each and its contract end
questions.listen: A contract end within the year is a migration with a deadline, for the provider and for every tenant.
questions.probe: What will you tell tenants whose service sits on the platform that is changing?

questions.q: What does it cost to run one tenant today, and what margin does each service leave?
questions.why: Margin per service decides which services to keep, move or drop.
questions.need: Cost and margin per service are known
questions.how: Work out the cost of one standard tenant with finance
questions.listen: A provider that cannot price one tenant cannot compete on price: the cost model is the first deliverable.
questions.probe: Which service loses money today, and why is it still offered?

questions.q: How many tenants, regions and clusters do you run, and how are tenants kept apart today?
questions.why: Scale, and the way tenants are separated, shape the design.
questions.need: Tenants, regions and isolation methods are listed
questions.how: List tenants per region with how each is isolated
questions.listen: Separation by convention rather than by construction is a risk with every new tenant.
questions.probe: Has one tenant ever seen or affected another, and how?

questions.q: Can tenants bring their own address ranges, and how are their networks built today?
questions.why: Tenants moving in want to keep their addresses; overlapping ranges need virtual networks.
questions.need: Tenants get their own virtual networks with their own addressing
questions.how: Count tenants that would need overlapping address ranges
questions.listen: Re-addressing every tenant on arrival kills migrations; virtual networks per tenant avoid it.
questions.probe: How long does it take today to set up a new tenant's network?

questions.q: How is usage measured per tenant, and how does it reach billing?
questions.why: Usage that is not metered is not billed.
questions.need: Usage per tenant is metered and exported to billing
questions.how: Trace one tenant's usage from the platform to the invoice
questions.listen: Billing from spreadsheets loses revenue and starts disputes; metering by the platform ends both.
questions.probe: How many billing disputes did you have last quarter, and over what?

questions.q: How are tenants' workloads protected and recovered, and is recovery a service they pay for?
questions.why: Recovery is both a duty and a service to sell.
questions.need: Tenant recovery is defined, tested and offered as a service
questions.how: List tenants with recovery and how it is tested
questions.listen: Recovery sold as a service with tested targets is a margin line, not a cost.
questions.probe: When was a tenant last restored, and how long did it take?

questions.q: Can tenants create and manage their own machines, networks and users, within limits you set?
questions.why: Self-service within guardrails is what tenants compare with the public cloud.
questions.need: Tenants serve themselves within quotas and policies
questions.how: List what tenants can do alone today and what needs a ticket
questions.listen: Tickets for every change cost the provider staff and the tenant time; quotas keep control without them.
questions.probe: Which tenant request takes your team the most time each month?

questions.q: How long does it take to onboard a new tenant, from contract to first machine?
questions.why: Onboarding time is both a sales argument and a cost.
questions.need: New tenants are onboarded by an automated workflow
questions.listen: Days of manual work per tenant limit growth; onboarding by workflow or API is the step up.
questions.probe: How many tenants could you onboard next month if they all signed?

questions.q: Which services beyond machines do tenants ask for: recovery, backup, Kubernetes, GPUs, object storage, desktops?
questions.why: Services of higher value raise the revenue per tenant.
questions.need: The services tenants ask for are listed with their demand
questions.how: Collect last year's requests that could not be served
questions.listen: Requests turned away are revenue lost to the large public clouds; each is a candidate service.
questions.probe: Which service did you lose a tenant over?

questions.q: Must tenant data stay in the country, and can you prove where it is and who can reach it?
questions.why: Sovereignty is a reason tenants choose a local provider.
questions.need: Data location and access can be proven per tenant
questions.how: Ask which tenants need proof of location, and in what form
questions.listen: Proof on demand, not a promise in a contract, is what regulated tenants and public bodies ask for.
questions.probe: Which tenants fall under public-sector cloud rules, and which qualifications do those rules require?

questions.q: How do tenants move to you from another platform, and who does the work?
questions.why: Easy moves win tenants; hard ones keep them where they are.
questions.need: A repeatable path moves tenants in from other platforms
questions.how: Agree a standard migration offer with tools and a price
questions.listen: A packaged migration at a fixed price wins tenants from providers that cannot move them.
questions.probe: How many tenants would move this year if the move were simple and priced?

questions.q: How are upgrades and maintenance done without disturbing tenants?
questions.why: Maintenance windows across many tenants are hard to agree.
questions.need: Platform upgrades run without tenant downtime
questions.how: Review the last upgrade and the tenants it affected
questions.listen: Rolling upgrades with no tenant downtime remove the hardest negotiation a provider has.
questions.probe: When did a maintenance window last cost you a tenant's goodwill?

questions.q: Which certifications and audits must the platform pass for your tenants?
questions.why: Certifications are the price of entry for regulated tenants.
questions.need: Required certifications are listed with their evidence
questions.how: List the certifications held and those tenants ask for
questions.listen: Each certification is evidence to produce every year; a platform that reports it continuously saves weeks.
questions.probe: Which certification would open a new market for you?

questions.q: How is your own staff's access to tenant environments controlled and recorded?
questions.why: Tenants and auditors ask who at the provider can reach their data.
questions.need: Staff reach tenant environments only when needed, and every access is recorded
questions.how: Give staff personal accounts with access granted per task, and keep a record tenants can be shown
questions.listen: Access per task with a record; "the operations team has admin everywhere" is what auditors ask about first.
questions.probe: Could you show a tenant who from your side touched their environment last month?
